Tag.equals and Tag.hashCode compare tag names exactly, so VIP and
vip are treated as different tags. A customer can then end up with
both, even though they mean the same thing to the user.

Let's make both methods ignore case. Person stores its tags in a
HashSet, which relies on equals and hashCode, so tags differing
only in case are now treated as duplicates everywhere.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag command: Show a note for duplicate tags
commitResults.messageBody:
Tagging a customer with a tag they already have shows the same
success message as adding a new tag, so users cannot tell that
nothing changed.

Let's show an informative note instead, and leave the customer
unchanged. This also covers tags that differ only in case, now
that tags are compared case-insensitively.

commitResults.messageBody:
The manual testing appendix has no steps for the tag command, so testers
cannot check its valid and invalid inputs systematically.

duplicate tags, invalid tags, repeated prefixes and invalid indexes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag command: Match untag's format and index errors
commitResults.messageBody:
The tag command shows AB3's "Invalid command format!" message and
its full usage text for every format or index problem. The untag
command shows a short format error, or a specific invalid-index
message. The team spec gives the same "Invalid index!" wording for
both, so the two commands report the same mistake differently.

Let's give tag a short format message in untag's style, and move the
invalid-index message into Messages so that tag and untag share one
copy. Tag now parses the tag before the index, as untag does, so both
commands show the same error for the same input.

Untag only switches to the shared constant. Its behaviour and
messages are unchanged.

A customer who cancels a preorder still needs to stay in the
contact list, but the only way to remove an order is to delete
the whole customer.

Let's add a deleteorder command that removes only the preorder of
the customer at a displayed index. The customer's contact details
and tags stay unchanged, and the current filter is kept, matching
delete and order.

The deleteorder command needs its user input parsed into a
DeleteOrderCommand.

Let's add DeleteOrderCommandParser, which works like
DeleteCommandParser and accepts a single positive index. Empty,
zero, negative, non-numeric, overflowing and extra arguments are
all rejected with the command's usage message.

DeleteOrderCommand and its parser exist, but the app does not
recognise the deleteorder command word yet.

Let's add it to AddressBookParser next to delete, and test that
the command word is dispatched to DeleteOrderCommandParser.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the current filter after tagging a person
commitResults.messageBody:
The tag command shows the full person list after adding a tag, so a
user who tagged a customer from find results loses those results.
untag, order and deleteorder all keep the current filter instead.

Let's keep the current filter after tagging, so that tag behaves like
the other commands that change a displayed person.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show which tag was added to whom after tagging
commitResults.messageBody:
The tag command replies with the person's full details, so the user
must scan a long message to confirm which tag was added. untag replies
with a short message naming the tag and the person instead.

Let's reply with "Added tag(s) [TAG] to NAME", mirroring untag's
"Removed tag(s) [TAG] from NAME", and keep the duplicate tag message.
Let's also document the message and common errors in the UG and DG.

The deleteorder command was merged without command tests, so its
success, failure and filtered-list behaviour is not checked
automatically.

Let's add DeleteOrderCommandTest, modelled on DeleteCommandTest. It
covers deleting a preorder from the full and the filtered list (the
filter is kept), a customer with no preorder, out-of-range indexes,
equals and toString.

Let's describe the preorder chips instead, matching the wording of
the order command's testing steps.

and preserving data after rejected updates. Keep ordinary equality
case-sensitive so display capitalization edits remain detectable.
